   2. Abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R134">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.play()` (with auto-rewind enabled) when the animation's effective playback rate is negative, its associated effect end is positive infinity, and its current time is unresolved, less than or equal to zero, or greater than the associated effect end must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort playback.</description>
    <spec_quote>If animation’s [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate) < 0, and animation’s [current time](#animation-current-time) is *either*: * [unresolved](#unresolved), or * less than or equal to zero, or * greater than [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end),
   :   If [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end) is positive infinity,
       :   throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
           and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R135">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.pause()` when the animation's current time is unresolved, its playback rate is negative, and its associated effect end is positive infinity must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort pausing.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. If the animation’s [current time](#animation-current-time) is [unresolved](#unresolved),
   perform the steps according to the first matching condition below:

   If animation’s [playback rate](#playback-rate) is ≥ 0,
   :   Set seek time to zero.

   Otherwise,
   :   If [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end) for animation is positive infinity,
       :   throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
           and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R136">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.finish()` when the animation's effective playback rate is zero must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort the operation.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If animation’s [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate) is zero,
   or if animation’s effective playback rate > 0
   and [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end) is infinity,
   throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
   and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R137">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.finish()` when the animation's effective playback rate is greater than zero and its associated effect end is positive infinity must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort the operation.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If animation’s [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate) is zero,
   or if animation’s effective playback rate > 0
   and [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end) is infinity,
   throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
   and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R138">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.cancel()` on an animation whose `playState` is not `"idle"` must reject its current `finished` promise with an `AbortError` `DOMException`.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If animation’s [play state](#animation-play-state) is *not* [idle](#play-state-idle),
   perform the following steps:

   1. Run the procedure to [reset an animation’s pending tasks](#animation-reset-an-animations-pending-tasks)
      on animation.
   2. Reject the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      with a `DOMException` named "`AbortError`".</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R139">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>When canceling a non-idle animation rejects its current `finished` promise, the promise's `[[PromiseIsHandled]]` internal slot must be set to `true` so that an unhandled rejection is not reported.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot
      of the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R140">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.cancel()` on an animation that has a pending play task or pending pause task must reject its current `ready` promise with an `AbortError` `DOMException`.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. Reject
   animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
   with a `DOMException` named "`AbortError`".</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R141">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>When resetting an animation's pending tasks rejects its current `ready` promise, the promise's `[[PromiseIsHandled]]` internal slot must be set to `true` so that an unhandled rejection is not reported.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot of animation’s
   [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise) to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R142">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.reverse()` when the animation has no associated timeline or its associated timeline is inactive must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort the operation.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If there is no [timeline](#timeline) associated with animation,
   or the associated timeline is [inactive](#inactive-timeline)
   throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
   and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R143">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>If invoking the play procedure during `Animation.reverse()` throws an exception (such as when the inverted playback rate is negative with an infinite effect end and unresolved or non-positive current time), `reverse()` must restore the animation's pending playback rate to its original value and propagate the exception.</description>
    <spec_quote>If the steps to [play an animation](#play-an-animation) throw an exception,
   set animation’s [pending playback rate](#pending-playback-rate)
   to original pending playback rate
   and propagate the exception.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R144">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.commitStyles()` when any effect target is not an element capable of having a `style` attribute (such as a pseudo-element or an element without style attribute support) must throw a `NoModificationAllowedError` `DOMException` and abort the operation.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If target is not an element capable of having
      a style attribute [[CSS-STYLE-ATTR]](#biblio-css-style-attr "CSS Style Attributes")
      (for example, it is a pseudo-element
      or is an element in a document format
      for which style attributes are not defined)
      throw a "`NoModificationAllowedError`" `DOMException`
      and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R145">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.commitStyles()` when any effect target is not being rendered after applying pending style changes (e.g., disconnected or within a `display: none` subtree) must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort the operation.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If, after applying any pending style changes,
      target is not being rendered,
      throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
      and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R146">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Updating an `AnimationEffect`'s timing (via `updateTiming()`, `KeyframeEffect` construction, or `Element.animate()`) with an `iterationStart` value less than zero must throw a `TypeError` and abort without applying timing changes.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If the `iterationStart` member of input
   exists and is less than zero,
   throw a `TypeError` and abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R147">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Updating an `AnimationEffect`'s timing with an `iterations` value that is less than zero or `NaN` must throw a `TypeError` and abort without applying timing changes.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If the `iterations` member of input exists,
   and is less than zero or is the value `NaN`,
   throw a `TypeError` and abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R148">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Updating an `AnimationEffect`'s timing with a numeric `duration` value that is less than zero or `NaN` must throw a `TypeError` and abort without applying timing changes.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. If the `duration` member of input exists,
   and is less than zero, is the value `NaN`,
   or is a string other than the lowercase `auto`,
   throw a `TypeError` and abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R149">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Updating an `AnimationEffect`'s timing with a string `duration` value other than the lowercase string `"auto"` must throw a `TypeError` and abort without applying timing changes.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. If the `duration` member of input exists,
   and is less than zero, is the value `NaN`,
   or is a string other than the lowercase `auto`,
   throw a `TypeError` and abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R150">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Updating an `AnimationEffect`'s timing with an `easing` string that cannot be parsed as a CSS `<easing-function>` must throw a `TypeError` and abort without applying timing changes.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. If the `easing` member of input exists
   but cannot be parsed using the <easing-function> production
   [[CSS-EASING-1]](#biblio-css-easing-1 "CSS Easing Functions Level 1"),
   throw a `TypeError` and abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R151">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Setting `KeyframeEffect.pseudoElement` to a non-null string that is an invalid `<pseudo-element-selector>` (including syntactically invalid or unsupported pseudo-elements) must throw a `SyntaxError` `DOMException` and leave the current `pseudoElement` unchanged.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If value is not `null`
       and is an invalid <pseudo-element-selector>,

       1. Throw a `DOMException`
          with error name "`SyntaxError`".
       2. Abort.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R152">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Constructing a `KeyframeEffect` (or invoking `Element.animate()`) with a `KeyframeEffectOptions` object whose `pseudoElement` property is non-null and an invalid `<pseudo-element-selector>` must throw a `SyntaxError` `DOMException` and abort construction.</description>
    <spec_quote>When assigning this property,
           the error-handling defined for
           the `pseudoElement` setter on the interface
           is applied.
           If the setter requires an exception to be thrown,
           this procedure must throw the same exception
           and abort all further steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R153">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animatable.getAnimations(options)` with a non-null `pseudoElement` option that is an invalid `<pseudo-element-selector>` must throw a `SyntaxError` `DOMException`.</description>
    <spec_quote>`DOMException` of type "`SyntaxError`"
    :   Raised if the `pseudoElement` option
        is not `null` and is an invalid <pseudo-element-selector>.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R154">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>If `KeyframeEffect.setKeyframes()` throws an exception while processing the `keyframes` argument, the effect's existing keyframes must remain unmodified.</description>
    <spec_quote>If that procedure throws an exception,
        this effect’s keyframes are not modified.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R155">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>During keyframe argument processing, if an ECMAScript operation on the input (such as accessing `Symbol.iterator`, iterating, or reading a keyframe property via a getter) results in an abrupt completion, the thrown exception must be propagated and keyframe processing aborted.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If result is
   an abrupt completion,
   throw the exception contained in the [[value]] field of result
   and abort the procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R156">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>When processing an iterable `keyframes` argument, if the iterator yields an item whose type is not `Undefined`, `Null`, or `Object` (such as a primitive number, string, or boolean), a `TypeError` must be thrown and processing aborted.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. If Type(nextItem) is not `Undefined`, `Null` or `Object`,
             then throw a `TypeError` and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R157">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>When processing a `keyframes` argument, if the processed keyframes are not loosely sorted in ascending order by their non-null `offset` values, a `TypeError` must be thrown and processing aborted.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. If processed keyframes is not [loosely sorted by offset](#loosely-sorted-by-offset),
   throw a `TypeError` and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R158">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>When processing a `keyframes` argument, if any keyframe has a non-null `offset` value less than `0` or greater than `1`, a `TypeError` must be thrown and processing aborted.</description>
    <spec_quote>7. If there exist any [keyframe](#keyframe) in processed keyframes
   whose [keyframe offset](#keyframe-offset) is non-null
   and less than zero or greater than one,
   throw a `TypeError` and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R159">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>When processing a `keyframes` argument, if a CSS property value in a keyframe is invalid according to that property's syntax, the property-value pair must be discarded without throwing an exception.</description>
    <spec_quote>If the property value is invalid
      according to the syntax for the property,
      discard the property-value pair.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R160">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>When processing a `keyframes` argument, if the `easing` property on any processed keyframe fails to parse as a CSS `<easing-function>`, a `TypeError` must be thrown and processing aborted.</description>
    <spec_quote>If parsing the `easing` property fails,
      throw a `TypeError` and abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R161">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>When processing a property-indexed `keyframes` argument, if any excess unused value in the `easing` list fails to parse as a CSS `<easing-function>`, a `TypeError` must be thrown and processing aborted.</description>
    <spec_quote>9. Parse each of the values in unused easings
   using the CSS syntax defined for
   the `easing` member of the `EffectTiming` dictionary,
   and if any of the values fail to parse,
   throw a `TypeError` and abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R162">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Any dynamic change made to any part of the Web Animations model must immediately update the entire timing model and any dependent styles.</description>
    <spec_quote>Changes made to any part of the model
cause the entire timing model to be updated
and any dependent style.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R163">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Invoking constructors or methods, or getting or setting attributes on Web Animations API interfaces must not trigger a style change event unless explicitly stated otherwise by the specification.</description>
    <spec_quote>Unless otherwise stated,
invoking the methods or constructors,
or getting or setting the members
of interfaces defined in the [Web Animations API](#web-animations-api)
does *not* produce a style change event.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R164">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.commitStyles()` must trigger a style change event so pending style changes are flushed before evaluating rendering state and committing styles.</description>
    <spec_quote>Unlike most other methods defined on this interface,
    calling this method *does* trigger a style change event
    (see [§ 6.13 Model liveness](#model-liveness)).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R165">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Calling `Animatable.getAnimations()` must trigger a style change event for the target element so the returned list reflects all pending style changes.</description>
    <spec_quote>Calling this method triggers
    a style change event for the [target element](#effect-target-target-element).
    As a result, the returned list reflects the state
    *after* applying any pending style changes to animation
    such as changes to animation-related style properties
    that have yet to be processed.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R166">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Calling `DocumentOrShadowRoot.getAnimations()` must trigger a style change event for the document so the returned list reflects all pending style changes.</description>
    <spec_quote>Calling this method triggers a style change event for the document.
    As a result, the returned list reflects the state
    *after* applying any pending style changes to animation
    such as changes to animation-related style properties
    that have yet to be processed.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R167">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Computed keyframes must remain live and behave as if recalculated every time an effect value is computed, dynamically reflecting changes to contextual computed styles such as `font-size`, custom properties, `writing-mode`, or `direction`.</description>
    <spec_quote>Note that [computed keyframes](#computed-keyframes) are “live”:
user-agents behave as if they are recreated
every time the [effect value](#effect-value) is calculated.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R168">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>A `DocumentTimeline`'s `currentTime` must remain fixed to the offset from the `now` timestamp provided by the most recent `update animations and send events` run, rather than advancing between animation frames.</description>
    <spec_quote>A document timeline is a type of [timeline](#timeline)
that is [associated with a document](#timeline-associated-with-a-document)
and whose [current time](#timeline-current-time) is calculated
as a fixed offset from the now timestamp provided
each time the [update animations and send events](#update-animations-and-send-events) procedure is run.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R169">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Dynamically modifying timing properties or adding or removing animations or animation effects must update the current animation frame without creating a new animation frame.</description>
    <spec_quote>Changes to the timing properties of [animations](#concept-animation) or [animation effects](#animation-effect),
or the addition and removal of the objects can
cause the output of the timing or animation model to change,
but these operations in themselves do not create a new [animation frame](#animation-frame);
rather they merely update the current animation frame.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R170">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>When the `Document` associated with a `DocumentTimeline` is not an active document, the timeline must transition to the inactive state and report an unresolved (`null`) `currentTime`.</description>
    <spec_quote>A [document timeline](#document-timeline) that is associated
with a `Document` that is not an active document
is also considered to be [inactive](#inactive-timeline).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R171">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>A document's default document timeline (`document.timeline`) must persist as the same instance for the lifetime of the document, including across calls to `document.open()`.</description>
    <spec_quote>The [default document timeline](#document-default-document-timeline) is unique to each document
and persists for the lifetime of the document,
including calls to document.open() [[HTML]](#biblio-html "HTML Standard").</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R172">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Setting an animation's `timeline` to the same timeline object it already has must abort without modifying hold time or updating finished state.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If new timeline is the same object as old timeline,
   abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R173">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>When changing an animation's `timeline` to a different timeline while its `start time` is resolved, its `hold time` must be cleared (made unresolved) so its finished state is re-evaluated against the new timeline.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. If the [start time](#animation-start-time) of animation is [resolved](#unresolved),
   make animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) unresolved.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R174">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Changing an animation's `timeline` to a different timeline must run the update finished state procedure with `did seek` set to false and `synchronously notify` set to false.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. Run the procedure to
   [update an animation’s finished state](#update-an-animations-finished-state) for animation
   with the did seek flag set to false,
   and the synchronously notify flag set to false.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R175">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Setting an animation's `effect` to the same effect object it already has must abort without rescheduling pending tasks or updating finished state.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If new effect is the same object as old effect,
   abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R176">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>When changing an animation's associated `effect` while it has a pending pause task, that pending pause task must be rescheduled to run as soon as the animation is ready.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. If animation has a [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task),
   reschedule that task to run as soon as animation is [ready](#ready).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R177">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>When changing an animation's associated `effect` while it has a pending play task, that pending play task must be rescheduled to run as soon as the animation is ready to play the new effect.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. If animation has a [pending play task](#pending-play-task),
   reschedule that task to run as soon as
   animation is [ready](#ready) to play new effect.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R178">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Assigning a non-null `AnimationEffect` that is already associated with another animation to an animation's `effect` attribute must detach it from the previous animation by setting the previous animation's associated effect to `null`.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. If new effect is not `null`
   and if new effect is the [associated effect](#animation-associated-effect)
   of another [animation](#concept-animation), previous animation,
   run the procedure to [set the associated effect of an animation](#animation-set-the-associated-effect-of-an-animation)
   (this procedure)
   on previous animation,
   passing null as new effect.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R179">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Changing an animation's associated `effect` to a different effect must run the update finished state procedure with `did seek` set to false and `synchronously notify` set to false.</description>
    <spec_quote>7. Run the procedure to [update an animation’s finished state](#update-an-animations-finished-state)
   for animation with the did seek flag set to false,
   and the synchronously notify flag set to false.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R180">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Setting an animation's `currentTime` must invalidate its cached `previous current time` by making it unresolved.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. Make animation’s [previous current time](#previous-current-time) [unresolved](#unresolved).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R181">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Setting `currentTime` on an animation that has a pending pause task must synchronously complete the pause operation by setting hold time to the seek time, applying any pending playback rate, making start time unresolved, canceling the pending pause task, and resolving the current ready promise.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If animation has a [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task),
   synchronously complete the pause operation
   by performing the following steps:

   1. Set animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) to seek time.
   2. [Apply any pending playback rate](#apply-any-pending-playback-rate) to animation.
   3. Make animation’s [start time](#animation-start-time) [unresolved](#unresolved).
   4. Cancel the [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task).
   5. Resolve
      animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
      with animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R182">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Setting an animation's `startTime` must synchronously apply any pending playback rate on the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. [Apply any pending playback rate](#apply-any-pending-playback-rate) on animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R183">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Setting an animation's `startTime` while it has a pending play task or pending pause task must cancel that pending task and resolve the animation's current ready promise with the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>7. If animation has a [pending play task](#pending-play-task) or a [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task),
   cancel that task and resolve
   animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
   with animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R184">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>An animation's `ready` promise must be replaced with a new Promise object whenever the animation queues a pending play task or pending pause task while not previously having a pending task.</description>
    <spec_quote>The object is replaced with a new Promise object
every time the animation queues
a [pending play task](#pending-play-task) or a [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task)
when it previously did not have a pending task</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R185">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Resetting an animation's pending tasks during cancellation must reject its current ready promise with an `AbortError` `DOMException` (marked as handled) and replace it with a new resolved Promise for the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. Reject
   animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
   with a `DOMException` named "`AbortError`".
6. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot of animation’s
   [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise) to true.
7. Let animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise) be the result of
   creating a new resolved Promise object
   with value animation
   in the relevant Realm of animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R186">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>When an animation leaves the `finished` play state and its `current finished promise` is already resolved, its `finished` promise must be replaced with a new pending Promise in the animation's relevant Realm.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. If current finished state is false
   and animation’s [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise) is already resolved,
   set animation’s current finished promise to
   a new promise in the relevant Realm of animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R187">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Canceling an animation that is not in the `idle` play state must reject its `current finished promise` with an `AbortError` `DOMException` (marked as handled) and replace it with a new pending Promise.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. Reject the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      with a `DOMException` named "`AbortError`".
   3. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot
      of the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      to true.
   4. Let [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise) be
      a new promise in the relevant Realm of animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R188">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Every modification to an animation object or the timing properties of its associated effect must check the finished boundary using the update finished state procedure.</description>
    <spec_quote>The crossing of this boundary
is checked on each modification to the animation object
or the timing properties of its [associated effect](#animation-associated-effect)
using the procedure to [update an animation’s finished state](#update-an-animations-finished-state) defined below.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R189">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>If an animation leaves the `finished` play state due to a dynamic change before its queued asynchronous finish notification microtask executes, the finish notification steps must abort without resolving the finished promise or queueing a finish event.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If animation’s [play state](#animation-play-state)
         is not equal to [finished](#play-state-finished),
         abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R190">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>When updating an animation's finished state with `synchronously notify` set to true (such as via `finish()`), any already-queued microtask for the animation's finish notification steps must be canceled and the steps must run immediately.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If synchronously notify is true,
      cancel any queued microtask to run
      the [finish notification steps](#finish-notification-steps) for this animation,
      and run the finish notification steps immediately.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R191">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Setting an animation's `playbackRate` attribute directly must clear any `pending playback rate` previously set via `updatePlaybackRate()`.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Clear any [pending playback rate](#pending-playback-rate) on animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R192">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>If `Animation.reverse()` fails because playing the animation throws an exception, the animation's `pending playback rate` must be restored to its original value before propagating the exception.</description>
    <spec_quote>If the steps to [play an animation](#play-an-animation) throw an exception,
   set animation’s [pending playback rate](#pending-playback-rate)
   to original pending playback rate
   and propagate the exception.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R193">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Updating an `AnimationEffect`'s timing via `updateTiming()` must run the update finished state procedure on its associated animation (if any) with `did seek` and `synchronously notify` set to false.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. If effect is [associated with an animation](#animation-effect-associated-animation),
   run the procedure to [update an animation’s finished state](#update-an-animations-finished-state)
   for its associated animation
   with the did seek flag set to false,
   and the synchronously notify flag set to false.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R194">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Calling `AnimationEffect.updateTiming()` must only update timing properties for members present on the input dictionary and leave omitted timing properties unchanged.</description>
    <spec_quote>The timing properties corresponding to any members
        that do not exist on `timing`
        will *not* be modified.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R195">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>If `KeyframeEffect.setKeyframes()` throws an exception while processing the keyframes argument, the effect's existing keyframes must remain unmodified.</description>
    <spec_quote>If that procedure throws an exception,
        this effect’s keyframes are not modified.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R196">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Once a `KeyframeEffect` associated with a `CSSAnimation` has its keyframes replaced by a successful call to `setKeyframes()`, `getKeyframes()` must stop returning the CSSAnimation's computed keyframes and instead return the replaced keyframes with missing offsets computed.</description>
    <spec_quote>If this [keyframe effect](#keyframe-effect) is associated with a `CSSAnimation`, and its [keyframes](#keyframe) have not been replaced by a successful call to `setKeyframes()`,
       :   the [computed keyframes](#computed-keyframes) for this [keyframe effect](#keyframe-effect).

       Otherwise,
       :   the result of applying the procedure
           [compute missing keyframe offsets](#compute-missing-keyframe-offsets)
           to the [keyframes](#keyframe) for this [keyframe effect](#keyframe-effect).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R197">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>When an animation's `replaceState` is `removed`, its animation effects must be excluded from the effect stacks of their target properties.</description>
    <spec_quote>The [animation effects](#animation-effect) of an [animation](#concept-animation)
whose [replace state](#replace-state) is [removed](#removed-replace-state)
are not included in the [effect stacks](#effect-stack) of their [target properties](#target-property).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R198">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>An animation whose `replaceState` transitions to `removed` must no longer be considered a relevant animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>An [animation](#concept-animation) is relevant if:

* Its [associated effect](#animation-associated-effect) is [current](#current) *or* [in effect](#in-effect),
  *and*
* Its [replace state](#replace-state) is *not* [removed](#removed-replace-state).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R199">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>During `remove replaced animations`, any active replaceable animation whose target properties are all targeted by higher composite-order replaceable animations must have its `replaceState` set to `removed`.</description>
    <spec_quote>When asked to remove replaced animations
for a `Document`, doc,
then for every [animation](#concept-animation), animation, that:

* has an [associated](#animation-effect-associated-animation) [animation effect](#animation-effect)
  whose [effect target](#keyframe-effect-effect-target) is a descendant of doc, and
* is [replaceable](#replaceable-animation), and
* has a [replace state](#replace-state) of [active](#active-replace-state), and
* for which there exists for each [target property](#target-property)
  of every [animation effect](#animation-effect)
  [associated](#animation-effect-associated-animation) with animation,
  an animation effect associated with a [replaceable](#replaceable-animation) [animation](#concept-animation)
  with a higher [composite order](#animation-composite-order) than animation
  that includes the same target property

perform the following steps:

1. Set animation’s [replace state](#replace-state) to [removed](#removed-replace-state).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R200">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.persist()` must set the animation's `replaceState` to `persisted`, preventing automatic replacement removal or restoring a previously removed animation's effects.</description>
    <spec_quote>Sets this animation’s [replace state](#replace-state)
    to [persisted](#persisted-replace-state).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R201">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>The user agent must act as if `will-change` includes a target property if and only if at least one animation effect targeting that property is `current` or `in effect` and its associated animation's `replaceState` is not `removed`.</description>
    <spec_quote>For every property targeted by at least one [animation effect](#animation-effect)
that is [current](#current) or [in effect](#in-effect),
and which is associated with an [animation](#concept-animation)
whose [replace state](#replace-state) is *not* [removed](#removed-replace-state),
the user agent must act as if
the will-change property [[css-will-change-1]](#biblio-css-will-change-1 "CSS Will Change Module Level 1") on the [effect target](#keyframe-effect-effect-target)
includes the property.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R202">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>During `update animations and send events`, the document's pending animation event queue must be copied and cleared before dispatching the events so events queued during dispatch are deferred to subsequent updates.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. Let events to dispatch be a copy of doc’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue).
5. Clear doc’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R203">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Prior to establishing the HTML time origin for its associated document, a document timeline must be inactive.</description>
    <spec_quote>Prior to establishing the time origin for its associated document,
a [document timeline](#document-timeline) is [inactive](#inactive-timeline).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R204">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>A document timeline associated with a `Document` that is not an HTML active document must be inactive (returning `null` for `currentTime`).</description>
    <spec_quote>A [document timeline](#document-timeline) that is associated
with a `Document` that is not an active document
is also considered to be [inactive](#inactive-timeline).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R205">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>A document's default document timeline (`document.timeline`) must persist as the same instance for the lifetime of the document, including across calls to `document.open()`.</description>
    <spec_quote>The [default document timeline](#document-default-document-timeline) is unique to each document
and persists for the lifetime of the document,
including calls to document.open() [[HTML]](#biblio-html "HTML Standard").</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R206">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>During the `update animations and send events` procedure, the user agent must perform a microtask checkpoint before dispatching queued animation events so that promise microtasks from timeline updates run prior to animation event listeners.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. Perform a microtask checkpoint.

   Note: This is to ensure that any microtasks queued up
   as a result of resolving or rejecting Promise objects
   as part of updating timelines in the previous step,
   run their callbacks prior to dispatching animation events.
4. Let events to dispatch be a copy of doc’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue).
5. Clear doc’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue).
6. Perform a stable sort of the [animation events](#animation-events) in events to dispatch
   as follows:

   1. Sort the events by their [scheduled event time](#scheduled-event-time)
      such that events that were scheduled to occur earlier
      sort before events scheduled to occur later,
      and events whose scheduled event time is [unresolved](#unresolved)
      sort before events with a resolved
      scheduled event time.
   2. Within events with equal [scheduled event times](#scheduled-event-time),
      sort by their [composite order](#animation-composite-order).

      Note: The purpose of sorting events is to ensure that, as best possible,
      even on devices with differing capabilities
      and hence different frame rates,
      events are dispatched in a consistent order.

      Note: The requirement for the sort to be a stable sort
      is because sometimes multiple events can be queued
      with the same scheduled event time.
      For example, a CSS animation with a duration of zero would dispatch
      both an `animationstart` and an `animationend` event
      with the same scheuled event time,
      and the order of these events should be preserved.
7. Dispatch each of the events in events to dispatch at their
   corresponding target using the order established in the previous step.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R207">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When an animation finishes without a document for timing, the user agent must queue a task on the HTML DOM manipulation task source to dispatch the `finish` event at the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>7. If animation has a [document for timing](#animation-document-for-timing),
         then append finishEvent
         to its document for timing’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue)
         along with its target, animation.
         For the [scheduled event time](#scheduled-event-time),
         use the result of
         [converting](#animation-time-to-origin-relative-time)
         animation’s [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end)
         to an origin-relative time.

         Otherwise,
         queue a task to dispatch finishEvent at animation.
         The task source for this task is
         the DOM manipulation task source.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R208">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When canceling a non-idle animation, the user agent must set the `[[PromiseIsHandled]]` internal slot of the rejected `current finished promise` to `true` so that an unhandled promise rejection is not reported.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. Reject the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      with a `DOMException` named "`AbortError`".
   3. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot
      of the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R209">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When an animation is canceled without a document for timing, the user agent must queue a task on the HTML DOM manipulation task source to dispatch the `cancel` event at the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>10. If animation has a [document for timing](#animation-document-for-timing),
       then append cancelEvent to
       its document for timing’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue)
       along with its target, animation.
       If animation is associated with an [active timeline](#active-timeline)
       that defines a procedure to
       [convert
       timeline times to origin-relative time](#timeline-time-to-origin-relative-time),
       let the [scheduled event time](#scheduled-event-time) be
       the result of applying that procedure to timeline time.
       Otherwise, the scheduled event time is
       an [unresolved](#unresolved) [time value](#time-value).

       Otherwise,
       queue a task to dispatch cancelEvent at animation.
       The task source for this task is
       the DOM manipulation task source.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R210">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When resetting an animation's pending play or pause tasks, the user agent must set the `[[PromiseIsHandled]]` internal slot of the rejected `current ready promise` to `true` so that an unhandled promise rejection is not reported.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. Reject
   animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
   with a `DOMException` named "`AbortError`".
6. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot of animation’s
   [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise) to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R211">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The document's pending animation event queue and sorting order must integrate Web Animations playback events together with events from CSS Transitions and CSS Animations.</description>
    <spec_quote>Animation events include
the [animation playback events](#animation-playback-events) defined in this specification
as well as the events from CSS transitions [[CSS-TRANSITIONS-1]](#biblio-css-transitions-1 "CSS Transitions Module Level 1")
and events from CSS animations [[CSS-ANIMATIONS-1]](#biblio-css-animations-1 "CSS Animations Level 1").</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R212">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>For CSS custom properties registered via `registerProperty()` in the current global object with a syntax corresponding to a computed value type, the animation type must be by computed value derived from the property's registered syntax definition.</description>
    <spec_quote>For custom properties registered using
the `registerProperty()` method for the current global object,
the [animation type](#animation-type) is [by computed value](#by-computed-value),
derived from the type used in the property’s syntax definition.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R213">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When a CSS custom property is unregistered or its registered syntax has no corresponding computed value type (such as the universal syntax definition), its animation type must be discrete.</description>
    <spec_quote>Where there is no computed value type that corresponds
to the property’s specified syntax
(e.g. when the syntax is the universal syntax definition)
or when the custom property is not registered,
the animation type is [discrete](#discrete).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R214">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When computing property values for keyframes on a target element, the computed values of any CSS property dependencies referenced by a value (such as `font-size` for `em` units) must be calculated first.</description>
    <spec_quote>When [computing a property value](#compute-a-property-value),
the computed values of dependencies held by value
must be calculated *first*.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R215">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When computing keyframes, CSS logical properties must be converted into their equivalent physical properties based on the effect target's computed `writing-mode` and/or `direction`.</description>
    <spec_quote>For logical properties [[CSS-LOGICAL-1]](#biblio-css-logical-1 "CSS Logical Properties and Values Module Level 1"),
        add the equivalent physical properties [[CSS-WRITING-MODES-4]](#biblio-css-writing-modes-4 "CSS Writing Modes Level 4")
        based on the computed value of writing-mode and/or direction
        for the [effect target](#keyframe-effect-effect-target).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R216">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When expanding logical properties in a keyframe causes a conflict with a physical property targeting the same longhand property, the physical property must override the logical property.</description>
    <spec_quote>If conflicts arise when expanding shorthand properties
      or replacing logical properties with physical properties,
      apply the following rules in order until the conflict is resolved:

      1. Longhand properties override shorthand properties
         (e.g. border-top-color overrides border-top).
      2. Shorthand properties with fewer longhand components
         override those with more longhand components
         (e.g. border-top overrides border-color).
      3. Physical properties override logical properties.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R217">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Applying a composited animation value to a CSS target property must insert the specified value into the CSS cascade at the level defined for the class of the highest-composite-order animation in the effect stack, defaulting to the Animation Origin of the cascade.</description>
    <spec_quote>Applying a [composited value](#composited-value) to a [target property](#target-property)
is achieved by adding a specified value to the CSS cascade.

The level of the cascade to which this specified value is added
depends on the [class](#animation-class) of the [animation](#concept-animation)
[associated with](#animation-effect-associated-animation)
the effect with the highest composite order in the [effect stack](#effect-stack)
for a given property.
By default, the specified value is added to
the Animation Origin of the cascade. [[CSS-CASCADE-3]](#biblio-css-cascade-3 "CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 3")</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R218">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>CSS animations with an owning element and CSS transitions with an owning element must not be considered replaceable and must not be automatically removed by the replaced animations procedure.</description>
    <spec_quote>An [animation](#concept-animation) is
replaceable
if *all* of the following conditions are true:

* The existence of the [animation](#concept-animation) is *not* prescribed by markup.
  That is, it is *not*
  a CSS animation with an owning element,
  nor a CSS transition with an owning element.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R219">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When an animation is automatically removed without a document for timing, the user agent must queue a task on the HTML DOM manipulation task source to dispatch the `remove` event at the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. If animation has a [document for timing](#animation-document-for-timing),
   then append removeEvent
   to its document for timing’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue)
   along with its target, animation.
   For the [scheduled event time](#scheduled-event-time),
   use the result of applying the procedure to convert
   [timeline time to origin-relative time](#timeline-time-to-origin-relative-time)
   to the [current time](#timeline-current-time) of the [timeline](#timeline)
   with which animation is associated.

   Otherwise,
   queue a task to dispatch removeEvent at animation.
   The task source for this task is
   the DOM manipulation task source.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R220">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>For every CSS property targeted by at least one current or in-effect animation effect whose animation does not have a replace state of `removed`, the user agent must apply the same side effects as if the CSS `will-change` property on the effect target included that property.</description>
    <spec_quote>For every property targeted by at least one [animation effect](#animation-effect)
that is [current](#current) or [in effect](#in-effect),
and which is associated with an [animation](#concept-animation)
whose [replace state](#replace-state) is *not* [removed](#removed-replace-state),
the user agent must act as if
the will-change property [[css-will-change-1]](#biblio-css-will-change-1 "CSS Will Change Module Level 1") on the [effect target](#keyframe-effect-effect-target)
includes the property.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R221">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>`Animation.commitStyles()` must be annotated with `[CEReactions]` so that custom element reactions are invoked when updating the target element's `style` attribute.</description>
    <spec_quote>[CEReactions]
  undefined commitStyles();</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R222">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>`Animation.commitStyles()` must write the current computed effect values of the animation's effects to the corresponding effect targets' inline `style` attribute.</description>
    <spec_quote>Writes the current [effect values](#effect-value)
    produced by this animation’s [animation effects](#animation-effect)
    to their corresponding [effect targets](#keyframe-effect-effect-target)' inline style
    using the [commit computed styles](#commit-computed-styles) procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R223">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.commitStyles()` must trigger a style change event.</description>
    <spec_quote>Unlike most other methods defined on this interface,
    calling this method *does* trigger a style change event
    (see [§ 6.13 Model liveness](#model-liveness)).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R224">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>If any effect target is not an element capable of having a CSS `style` attribute (such as a pseudo-element or an element without style attribute support), `Animation.commitStyles()` must throw a `NoModificationAllowedError` `DOMException`.</description>
    <spec_quote>If target is not an element capable of having
      a style attribute [[CSS-STYLE-ATTR]](#biblio-css-style-attr "CSS Style Attributes")
      (for example, it is a pseudo-element
      or is an element in a document format
      for which style attributes are not defined)
      throw a "`NoModificationAllowedError`" `DOMException`
      and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R225">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>If, after applying pending style changes, any effect target is not being rendered according to HTML, `Animation.commitStyles()` must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException`.</description>
    <spec_quote>If, after applying any pending style changes,
      target is not being rendered,
      throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
      and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R226">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>For `Animation.commitStyles()`, a connected element with `display: contents` that is not part of a `display: none` subtree must be treated as being rendered.</description>
    <spec_quote>For the purpose of this procedure,
      we assume that an element with display: contents
      that otherwise would have associated layout boxes
      (i.e. it is connected
      and not part of a display: none subtree)
      *is* being rendered.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R227">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Setting a target pseudo-selector to a non-null string that is an invalid CSS `<pseudo-element-selector>` must throw a `SyntaxError` `DOMException` and leave the target pseudo-selector unchanged.</description>
    <spec_quote>If value is not `null`
       and is an invalid <pseudo-element-selector>,

R233: Calling `Element.getAnimations()` must trigger a style change event for the target element so that pending animation-related style changes are reflected in the returned list. -> [COVERED by web-animations/interfaces/Animatable/getAnimations.html]
R234: The DOM `Document` interface must be extended with a readonly `timeline` attribute of type `DocumentTimeline`. -> [COVERED by web-animations/idlharness.window.js]
R235: The DOM `DocumentOrShadowRoot` mixin must expose `getAnimations()`, returning the relevant animations for the subtree of the `Document` or `ShadowRoot` on which it is called. -> [COVERED by web-animations/interfaces/DocumentOrShadowRoot/getAnimations.html]
R236: Calling `getAnimations()` on a `Document` or `ShadowRoot` must trigger a style change event for the document so that pending animation-related style changes are reflected in the returned list. -> [COVERED by web-animations/interfaces/DocumentOrShadowRoot/getAnimations.html]
R237: The DOM `Element` interface must include the `Animatable` interface mixin. -> [COVERED by web-animations/idlharness.window.js]
R238: Changes made to any part of the Web Animations model must immediately update the entire timing model and any dependent CSS styles. -> [COVERED by web-animations/interfaces/KeyframeEffect/setKeyframes.html]
R239: Unless otherwise stated by the specification, invoking Web Animations API methods or constructors, or getting or setting its interface members, must not produce a style change event. -> [COVERED by web-animations/interfaces/Animation/style-change-events.html]
